original_question: For any n ≥ 2, is there a simple orderable group of type Fn but not Fn+1 ?
target_in_paper: Question 3.4 in Section 3.3 (“Simple orderable groups”): “For any n ≥ 2, is there a simple orderable group of type F_n but not F_{n+1}?” ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper: it matches the exact quantifier n ≥ 2, the class of groups (simple orderable groups), and the precise finiteness-property separation being asked for, namely type F_n but not F_{n+1}. In substance, it is essentially Question 3.4 verbatim. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the notation should be expanded: the paper immediately defines “G is of type F_n” to mean that G admits a classifying space K(G,1) with finite n-skeleton. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
The quantifier is over integers n ≥ 2. The paper states this explicitly. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

If you want the question to be fully self-contained, it is helpful to spell out the complementary condition “not of type F_{n+1}” as meaning that G does not admit a K(G,1) with finite (n+1)-skeleton. This is the nearby definitional reformulation used by the paper’s notation. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The paper leaves “orderable” unqualified in Question 3.4, so a stand-alone rewrite should either keep that exact word or explicitly state which orderability notion is intended; the paper itself does not add further hypotheses here. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

There are no additional ambient choices or hidden parameters in the paper’s formulation: no ring or field, no degree or homogeneity assumptions, no operator definitions, and no asymptotic clauses such as “for sufficiently large” appear in this question. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: For each integer n ≥ 2, does there exist a simple orderable group G that admits a classifying space K(G,1) with finite n-skeleton, but does not admit any classifying space K(G,1) with finite (n+1)-skeleton? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for each integer n ≥ 2, is there a simple orderable group of type F_n but not F_{n+1}? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Question 3.4 exactly, not a neighboring broader problem. The only nearby context needed to make it completely stand-alone is the sentence immediately before Question 3.4, where the paper defines type F_n and type F_∞. The paragraph after the question confirms the intended scope: the authors are asking specifically for a finiteness-property gap inside the class of simple orderable groups, noting that Hyde–Lodha supply finitely presented examples of type F_∞ and that analogous constructions exist once the orderability condition is dropped. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is just the official question with the notation F_n/F_{n+1} spelled out. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
